key_insight: Stitching artifacts can quietly hurt downstream segmentation even when generative image quality looks acceptable, and artifact-free 3D stitching offers only a modest edge over 2D.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical image generation workflows, evaluation must include downstream task performance, not just visual or FID-based quality, to avoid misleading results.
method: Compared cycleGAN-based style-transfer models with three stitching strategies.
Assessed perceptual quality and mitochondria segmentation performance on cryo-EM datasets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that FID did not detect subtle stitching artifacts, while downstream mitochondria segmentation captured meaningful performance differences across stitching methods and patch dimensionalities.
watch_item: 3D artifact-free stitching may improve outputs slightly, but the computational cost is high and benefits may not justify the added complexity in many settings.
paper_title: Stitching and dimensionality effects on large artificially generated volume datasets
